messages:
will (Support): raised a P1 from ACME — streaming responses over our /v1/stream endpoint get truncated in Safari Private Windows. Customer sees partial last event then connection stays open but no more data. ticket: https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/AI-987 :grimacing:

priya (SRE): thanks, dropping in. do we have request id / sample replay?

will (Support): pasted replay and headers from their environment:

```
GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-lite HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Accept: text/event-stream
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 13_4) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/16.4 Safari/605.1.15
Connection: keep-alive
```

Response observed (from customer tcp capture):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
X-Request-ID: req_abc123
\ndata: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello"}}]}\n\ndata: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":" world"}}]}\n\ndata: {"choices":[{"delta":{}}]}\n```

Then connection hangs for 30s, then Safari never fires the final `onmessage` for the last chunk in Private mode. Non-private Safari and Chrome both fine. Polyfill (eventsource-polyfill) made a difference for them.

priya (SRE): interesting — private mode + service worker? customer said they have a service worker that proxies analytics and sometimes rewrites `Cache-Control`. could be ServiceWorker streaming interaction in Safari PW. staging-bot: flagged to eng/runtime.

hao (Eng): quick thoughts: Safari in private windows disables or tightens disk storage and may buffer streams differently in the ServiceWorker fetch handler. If the SW does `response.clone()` and then calls `event.respondWith(streamedResponse)`, I've seen edge behavior where final chunk gets coalesced or delayed. Do we have reproducer without the customer's SW?

will (Support): they reproduced locally with their SW disabled — then stream completes OK in private mode. With SW enabled (simple pass-through), reproduce occurs. They attached a tiny repro repo: https://github.com/acme/safari-sse-repro (private).

priya (SRE): can you ask them for a minimal ServiceWorker snippet? also request the exact Safari build. if we can reproduce in our lab we can instrument the runtime to see if we end up sending zero-length chunk or drop `\r\n` boundary.

will (Support): SW snippet (sanitized):
```
self.addEventListener('fetch', e => {
  if (e.request.url.includes('/v1/stream')) {
    e.respondWith(fetch(e.request)); // pass-through
  }
});
```

hao (Eng): that's the simplest case. Safari PW + SW pass-through seems to change how the browser handles streamed responses from a chunked backend. two hypotheses: 1) the SW is buffering the response until the stream is "complete" and due to Private mode storage limits the OS swaps the buffer to memory and drops last event boundary; 2) Safari's EventSource implementation in PW expects a final `\n\n` terminated event and if the SW altered `Content-Length` / chunk framing it never triggers `dispatchEvent`.

priya (SRE): to triage: 1) ask the customer to capture a raw fetch response body via `fetch` + `body.getReader()` to see if frames arrive at the network layer. 2) try forcing `Cache-Control: no-store` on the upstream response (we already send no-cache but try no-store). 3) try sending explicit event separator `\n\n` and a small keepalive comment `: keepalive\n\n` after every message.

will (Support): sent steps to customer. they tried `: keepalive\n\n` and said it made the connection much more reliable but occasionally still dropped the final event.

hao (Eng): small kernel: add a safeguard on our side — if the runtime emits an SSE event we will append an extra keepalive comment and ensure the event ends with `\n\n`. also log last-byte timing for that request id so SRE can correlate. will that be acceptable?

priya (SRE): yes, please roll a small patch to the streaming middleware in staging. include a test that simulates a SW-pass-through client (we can run WebKitGTK headless in private-mode config).

hao (Eng): I'll land a quick change: add trailing `: _\n\n` after every event and a 250ms no-op flush after closing the chunk. doing now, will ping when staging build is up.

staging-bot: deploy started for commit sha:abcd1234 -> staging (runtime/streaming-mw), ETA ~7m

priya (SRE): once staging ready we'll run the repro suite with and without SW in PW. will you attach the `X-Request-ID` from the customer's logs so I can filter?

will (Support): gave `req_abc123` and the customer's timestamp. customer confirmed they can test staging if we provide an ephemeral URL.

hao (Eng): staging up: https://staging-stream.redwood.internal/stream-repro?token=tmp. ran repro with WebKit headless in Private-mode+SW pass-through — I can repro a dropped final onmessage ~1/20 runs. pushing an extra flush fix now.

staging-bot: deploy finished for commit sha:abcd1234 -> staging (success)

priya (SRE): ran 200 iterations — failure rate dropped to 0/200 with the flush + keepalive. lovely. will prepare a small postmortem note and recommended mitigation for customers that rely on SW.

will (Support): pinged ACME with staging URL and patch notes: "we added robust SSE termination handling: explicit keepalive comments and trailing flush to help Safari Private Window + ServiceWorker clients." they confirmed staging reduced failures in their tests. :thumbsup:

hao (Eng): follow-up action: add a KB entry under support about Safari PW + ServiceWorker SSE issues and recommended server-side keepalive/events termination. also add an automated test in our runtime CI using WebKit headless (private mode + SW pass-through) to catch regressions.

priya (SRE): agreed. marking P1 -> P2 for now since customer validated staging. will close after KB + CI test are added.

will (Support): closing loop with ACME and adding entries to ticket. thanks team. :cheers:
